It says the 0.85 line lies inside the range measured elsewhere for two cold runs (0.72 once), "so the test measures a second pair before it fails". The second pair only re-measures a pair that failed. A first pair that passes ends the test (lines 486-489), so one cold pair under 0.85 (and under 0.75 on the early rise on Linux) passes with no warm-up, and nothing re-measures it. The retry guards the other side: a working warm-up that reads near the line (0.74 in one macOS log). Row 509 states the open rate at its end, so this is wording only. Fix: say the second pair is for a working warm-up near the line, and that a pass is not measured again.

problems.text: macOS is the thin side and only the runner can show it. From the two logs I computed 0.659 and 0.741 for the asserted relation, so both pass, with 0.11 to spare in the worse one. There the warm-up only removes the first step (about 32 to 35 KB against 197 to 203 KB); the later drift of about 340 KB is the same in both runs and dilutes the ratio. The two cold rises in the logs differ by 1% (543,624 and 538,888 bytes), so a missing warm-up should read near 1.0 there. Two samples cannot give a failure rate; the row says this.

"While the 0.85 relation held" at sixteen copies is true of the two-pair sums only. In the logs of that run (u9chk-N2/res/t21x16.test.*.log, t25x16.test.*.log) all 8 final failures are the 0.75 relation, as stated, but 4 of 32 first pairs failed the 0.85 relation alone (0.89 and 0.90 on JDK 21). The stated cause fits the data: at sixteen copies the warm run took a median 3.9 s longer than the cold run on JDK 21 (about 0.7 s at four copies), which is the 3 s cap being reached, and fewer warm rounds raised the ratio (up to 0.86 with 3 to 15 rounds).
